findings.summary: Page 1 opens with storage summaries, recaps and best practices that depend on material taught later — Glacier lower on the same page and the storage-class table on page 2.
findings.evidence: Page 1 "Quick Recap" lists "**Archive** -> Glacier" and "Key Takeaways" says "Picking the right storage class cuts cost the most" and "Durability (11 nines) is not the same as availability" — the "S3 Glacier" section follows below, and the "5. S3 Storage Classes" table with the 99.99%/99.9%/99.5% availability column is on page 2.
findings.fix: Reorder page 1 so S3 Glacier and Storage Gateway are explained first and the Quick Recap, Key Takeaways and Best Practices blocks close the page; move the storage-class table from page 2 ahead of the takeaway that compares durability and availability.

findings.summary: Page 1 tells the reader to enable versioning and MFA Delete before either term is explained on page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 1 Best Practices: "Enable ==versioning== plus lifecycle rules" and "Turn on **MFA Delete** for critical buckets"; page 3 "7. Bucket Features" first defines "Versioning keeps every object version" and page 3 "6. S3 Security" defines "**MFA Delete** on versioned buckets".
findings.fix: Move the "7. Bucket Features" and "6. S3 Security" sections ahead of the page 1 best-practices list, or drop those two bullets from page 1 and keep the recommendations with the definitions on page 3.

findings.summary: The S3 storage class table understates the designed-for availability of S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive as 99.9%.
findings.evidence: ["Glacier Flexible","Archive minutes-hours","99.9%"],["Glacier Deep Archive","Long term lowest cost","99.9%"]
findings.fix: Change both rows' availability to 99.99% (AWS designs S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive for 11 nines durability and 99.99% availability); only S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval and Standard-IA are 99.9%.

findings.summary: A stateless/stateful firewall comparison is wedged between two storage sections on a storage page, and the same comparison is repeated in fuller form on page 5.
findings.evidence: Page 2 block order: "2. S3" → "10. NACL vs SG" (rows Type/Level/Rule) → "3. EFS"; page 5 repeats "6. SG vs NACL" with the same Type/Level/Rule rows plus Default/Order/Return Traffic.
findings.fix: Delete the "10. NACL vs SG" table from page 2 so S3 flows straight into EFS; keep only the fuller page 5 table.

findings.summary: The security block starts at section 5 (Key Security Services) on page 3, while its foundational sections 1-3 (Shared Responsibility, IAM, Policy Structure) only arrive on page 4.
findings.evidence: Page 2 ends with "AWS provides a ==shared responsibility model== and security services to protect resources."; page 3 then opens with "5. Key Security Services"; page 4 carries "1. Shared Responsibility", "2. IAM" and "3. Policy Structure".
findings.fix: Move page 4's sections 1-3 ahead of page 3's security services so the intro paragraph is followed by the shared responsibility model, then IAM, then policy structure, then the service table.

findings.summary: The block presented as an IAM "Policy Structure" is not a valid IAM policy document — it omits the required Statement array and the Version element.
findings.evidence: "3. Policy Structure" / "JSON document defining permissions and restrictions" / "Elements: Effect, Action, Resource, Condition" over the snippet starting `{ "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["s3:ListBucket"], ...`
findings.fix: Wrap the snippet as a real policy — `{"Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [{ "Effect": ..., "Action": ..., "Resource": ..., "Condition": ... }]}` — and add Version/Statement (and optionally Sid, Principal) to the list of policy elements.

findings.summary: The "5. Key Security Services" table is published twice, on page 3 and again on page 5, listing the same five services.
findings.evidence: Page 3: rows "{icon:iam} **IAM**" / "{icon:cloudtrail} **CloudTrail**" / "{icon:kms} **KMS**" / "{icon:waf} **WAF**" / "{icon:guardduty} **GuardDuty**"; page 5: rows "IAM", "CloudTrail", "KMS", "WAF", "GuardDuty" under the identical heading "5. Key Security Services".
findings.fix: Keep one copy (the page 3 version with icons) and delete the duplicate table from page 5.

findings.summary: The monitoring intro promised at the end of page 4 is followed by three more security sections before CloudWatch actually begins.

findings.fix: Move the security sections (SG vs NACL, Common Mistakes) to the end of page 4 with the rest of the security material, so the monitoring intro is immediately followed by "1. CloudWatch".

findings.summary: The storage comparison table labels FSx as SMB-only while simultaneously citing HPC as its use case, which FSx for Lustre serves over the Lustre/POSIX protocol, not SMB.
findings.evidence: ["FSx","File (SMB)","Yes","Windows, HPC"]
findings.fix: Change the Type cell to "File (SMB/NFS/Lustre)" — SMB applies to FSx for Windows File Server, while FSx for Lustre, NetApp ONTAP and OpenZFS use Lustre/NFS — matching the "SMB/Lustre" wording already used in the page 4 comparison table.
